selfResolutions.decision: Restore the copilot delete_file / delete_file_folder family additively
selfResolutions.rationale: Upstream retired both tools with no replacement. Census: DeleteFile / DeleteFileFolder = base 1, fork 1, upstream 0, merged 0 - upstream tools the fork still depends on. delete-file.ts is deleted SILENTLY (fork never modified it since base, so git takes the deletion with no conflict) and tool-schemas-v1.ts auto-merges to zero delete_file occurrences. Restoring additively is unconditionally safe on the upstream side.

selfResolutions.decision: Router and Evaluator adopt resolveProxiedModelCost; keep resolveBlockModelCost exported

Keeping the fork helper at these two call sites would therefore apply the margin TWICE on Router and Evaluator blocks. Upstream containing all of the fork helper's features is exactly the condition the human set on run 2026-08-06-4 Q1. Keep the export: the fork-only lib/billing/core/historical-workflow-reconciliation.ts still consumes it.

Q1-A.notes: Fork-first. Keep isPersonal, userHasPersonalWorkspace and the !isOrgAdmin && !isPersonal 403 cap verbatim. Upstream's new modules (billing-identity-lock, requireOrganizationOwnerId, disclosure-copy) are taken additively so the tree compiles, but the policy function's return shape stays the fork's. mustEdit on route.ts: it must keep passing isPersonal AND satisfy upstream's createWorkspace signature - add observedOrganizationId as a pass-through field rather than a decision input. Verify the WorkspaceCreationPolicy type in hooks/queries/workspace.ts still matches what the route returns.

Q1-B.notes: Upstream-first. Adopt #5918's policy end-to-end including observedOrganizationId and blockedReasonCode. The workspace.is_personal COLUMN stays in the schema and its non-policy consumers keep working (settings api-keys/secrets UI, lib/billing/authorization.ts, lib/channel-accounts.ts, the v1 admin import route) - only the policy function stops reading it. Drop userHasPersonalWorkspace from the creation path and drop the !isOrgAdmin && !isPersonal cap. Behaviour change to announce: plain Arena members can create additional organization workspaces. Verify lib/workspaces/create-workspace.ts still sets is_personal for a user's first workspace so the UI consumers do not all read false.

Q1-C.notes: Hybrid. Take upstream's structure - observedOrganizationId, requireOrganizationOwnerId, the billing-identity lock, blockedReasonCode and the new return shape - then re-add the fork's !isOrgAdmin && !isPersonal 403 guard on the !isBillingEnabled path only, sourcing isPersonal from userHasPersonalWorkspace. Return both observedOrganizationId and isPersonal so no consumer breaks. Most work of the three, and the only option that ends the structural divergence while preserving today's member restriction.

Q2-A.notes: Keep the sweep as upstream shipped it. lib/invitations/ is taken wholesale from the auto-merge - no directive needed there. invite.tsx must carry BOTH sides: upstream's buildMembershipNotice / buildWorkspaceMigrationNotice disclosure and useInvitationDetails, and the fork's auto-login effect plus useBrandConfig. Post-merge verification: accept an org invite in a scratch workspace and confirm organizationId and billedAccountUserId move as disclosed, and that the disclosure-outdated path renders rather than throwing.

Q2-B.notes: Disable the sweep. Take #5918's invitation refactor for everything else but neutralise the workspace-migration step inside the acceptance transaction in lib/invitations/core.ts, and suppress the migration notice in invite.tsx and disclosure-copy.ts so the UI does not promise a move that will not happen. Keep the disclosure-outdated guard itself intact - with an empty sweep set it is inert. This is a fork carve-out inside an actively developed upstream module: record it in extensibility-notes and expect to re-apply it every sync. Also add lib/invitations/ to merge-policy.forkFirst if this option is chosen.
